summary: Interpreted the new retained receipt (CheckRun a8e8732ff16b4c37b22e79408d1f066a: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 16 parsed observations, 0 parse errors) for the transfer question and used its operands to close that account. Indices 10-15 show the leader already matching the lagging transferee at its last index, the transfer accepted as a pending duty with the transferee staying StateFollower, a proposal rejected with ErrProposalDropped during the window, leadTransferee cleared after one election timeout with the leader still leading and proposals accepted again, and the retried transfer completing with the transferee leading at term 2 and the former leader a follower, so the transfer duty is delayed and bounded by the transferee's application lag rather than lost - conclusion holds with the defect claim refuted, and the cost (a proposal-rejection window whose length tracks that lag) is recorded as counterevidence rather than glossed over. I also corrected the construction-note knowledge entry under its existing id with changed_premise: the earlier statement described a draft-side run pending a receipt, and it now states the receipt-backed operands and its exact conditions. Finally, since all three answered questions exercise hand-built prefixes, I registered a new independent question - a randomized invariant sweep over elections, proposals, ticks, partitions, transfers and persist/apply cycles checking at-most-one-leader-per-term, no committed (index, term) ever contradicted, committed-index monotonicity and applied<=committed - and extended the same harness with its fourth case, for which a fresh isolated execution is now requested; the sweep's draft-side run reported 60 seeds x 60 steps, 459 elections, 446 proposals and 0 violations, recorded only as construction feedback since it is a holds-only result over a fixed event set and not a safety proof. Not yet done: the sweep omits configuration changes, joint configs and node restarts, and it has no receipt yet, so it cannot yet support any statement about a defect or about safety in general.
